trust_decision.summary: The client must not answer a server-requested mysql_clear_password authentication with the account password in cleartext unless the application opted in via enableCleartextPlugin or a custom authPlugins entry; the decision is enforced at three places: the AuthSwitchRequest dispatch (auth_switch.js:75), the initial-handshake direct-auth selection (client_handshake.js:105), and the new connection option (connection_config.js:154), with the specific error code preserved at client_handshake.js:343.

landing_point.why: The summary names the auth-plugin switch; this is where the server-controlled pluginName is read and immediately turned into a plugin choice at auth_switch.js:75, so it is the first place an engineer who read only the advisory would look.

fix_sites.entry_point: connection establishment via mysql.createConnection(), mysql.createPool() and the mysql2/promise wrappers, when the server sends AuthSwitchRequest/AuthNextFactor; also Connection#changeUser() (change_user.js:63-64 reuses this handshakeResult)
mysql.createConnection()/createPool() initial handshake when the server advertises mysql_clear_password in its hello packet (direct-auth optimisation that never sees an AuthSwitchRequest)
fix_sites.module_kind: handshake command - second implementation of the auth response

fix_sites.entry_point: same initial handshake; error normalisation in handshakeResult so the gate's MYSQL_CLEAR_PASSWORD_NOT_ENABLED code survives
ConnectionConfig option validation used by createConnection(), createPool() (pool_config.js:10) and the promise wrappers
ConnectionConfig assignment of enableCleartextPlugin, reached by every connection and pool route (plus URI query strings via parseUrl)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The direct-auth path at client_handshake.js:105-108 is already gated on a secure connection (ssl or socketPath) by canUseAuthMethodDirectly (client_handshake.js:203-213), and the project's own docs still say 'The initial handshake is always performed using mysql_native_password' (website/docs/documentation/authentication-switch.mdx:68), so a solver can argue that path is already protected and that the advisory only covers the auth-switch downgrade.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: caching_sha2_password full authentication over TLS/Unix socket (and sha256_password over TLS, sha256_password.js:42-48) legitimately writes the plaintext password to the wire; it is the default MySQL 8 auth path and a grep-level fix on the Buffer.from(`${password}\0`) pattern or a blanket refusal of cleartext would break normal secure-connection logins, as would flipping canUseAuthMethodDirectly for mysql_clear_password, which the pinned unit test asserts is true over SSL (test/unit/commands/test-client-handshake-auth.test.mts:186-192).

O6_input_shapes: server advertises mysql_clear_password in its hello packet (initial-handshake direct auth, client_handshake.js:105-108)
server sends AuthSwitchRequest with pluginName mysql_clear_password during the handshake (auth_switch.js:55)
server sends AuthNextFactor (marker 0x02) naming mysql_clear_password, including 2nd/3rd factor passwords (client_handshake.js:327-338)
enableCleartextPlugin absent, false or true (Boolean coercion, connection_config.js:154)
authPlugins object with an own mysql_clear_password property as implicit opt-in, versus an inherited/prototype property (auth_switch.js:14-22, 26-34)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a plugin-name gate inside authSwitchRequestMoreData, which re-invokes the stored connection._authPlugin on every AuthMoreData round without re-checking which plugin it is
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The gate lives only in authSwitchRequest, yet the same instance is invoked again from authSwitchRequestMoreData for multi-round plugins; a maintainer fixing credential leakage would plausibly mirror the check there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a gated wrapper factory in the public mysql2.authPlugins map so mysql_clear_password itself refuses to produce a token unless opted in
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: index.js:40 exports this map publicly as mysql2.authPlugins, so enforcing the opt-in at the public factory rather than at each call site is a natural maintainer choice.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: URI query-param handling/whitelisting for enableCleartextPlugin in parseUrl (e.g. refusing to let a connection URL turn cleartext auth on)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The repo already fixed query-param override of URL-defined options (#4162, Changelog.md:40), so a sibling parse/merge rule in the same function is realistic.

O9_family: insufficiently protected credentials / cleartext transmission of a password (CWE-522)

O10_build.language: JavaScript (CommonJS) with TypeScript typings and .mts tests
O10_build.toolchain: npm, Node >= 8 (package.json:50-52), poku test runner (package.json:11), tsx/typescript for .mts tests, rollup for the bundle
services: none for this behaviour: the gate test uses an in-process mock server via mysql.createServer; the wider integration suite needs a live MySQL (docker compose)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a pluginName === 'mysql_clear_password' guard inside authSwitchRequest and throw a plain Error (or flip canUseAuthMethodDirectly), leaving the initial-handshake direct-auth path, the enableCleartextPlugin option and the err.code preservation untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent but outside this advisory: sha256_password (lib/auth_plugins/sha256_password.js:42-48) and caching_sha2_password full auth (lib/auth_plugins/caching_sha2_password.js:73-81) also put the plaintext password on the wire when config.ssl/socketPath is set; recorded only as the coupled legitimate behaviour, not pursued.
